analysis: The candidate ran successfully but reduced validation HR@10 from 0.665 to 0.645, a decline of 0.020 (2 percentage points). Its best checkpoint occurred at epoch 25 of 45. Reject this modification and retain the 0.665 incumbent. Final-state identity initialization preserved the initial readout mapping, but learned depth fusion did not improve validation ranking in this trial; the result does not establish why. No test metrics were used.
code_summary: A causal NextItNet with 64 hidden units, eight gated local/dilated residual blocks, dilation schedule [1,2,4,8,1,2,4,8], kernel size 3, dropout 0.2, and channel-wise residual scales initialized to 0.1. The candidate concatenates masked states at depths 0, 4, and 8, then applies a bias-free 1×1 convolution initialized to select only the final state, followed by the existing LayerNorm and mask. Position-free embeddings, tied item scoring, interfaces, and all eight hyperparameters remain unchanged. Training and evaluation remain host-owned.
